title: Knowledge check: Express.js and Related Technologies

questions.prompt: In Express.js and Related Technologies, which statement best describes Express.js versus Node.js?
options: Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Keep the layers distinct: Node.js runs JavaScript and provides runtime APIs; Express builds request routing and middleware behavior on top of that runtime.
Choose static delivery, server rendering or a separate frontend according to the product need. Escape untrusted template output and do not expose private files through public asset paths.
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
questions.answer_key: Keep the layers distinct: Node.js runs JavaScript and provides runtime APIs; Express builds request routing and middleware behavior on top of that runtime.
questions.explanation: Keep the layers distinct: Node.js runs JavaScript and provides runtime APIs; Express builds request routing and middleware behavior on top of that runtime.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Express.js and Related Technologies?
options: Express is a web framework layered on the Node.js runtime. Start by tracing one HTTP request through a route handler, middleware, and response, and keep framework features separate from packages in the broader ecosystem.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.
questions.answer_key: Express is a web framework layered on the Node.js runtime. Start by tracing one HTTP request through a route handler, middleware, and response, and keep framework features separate from packages in the broader ecosystem.
questions.explanation: Express is a web framework layered on the Node.js runtime. Start by tracing one HTTP request through a route handler, middleware, and response, and keep framework features separate from packages in the broader ecosystem.

questions.prompt: A change related to Express.js and Related Technologies appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
